author: Chris Schommer
title: Colson Montgomery goes yard in win over Yankees
desc: Colson Montgomery went 2-for-3 in a win over the Yankees with a solo home run and one walk.
impact: Montgomery has flashed his power stroke of late, homering in three of his last four contests. The infielder offers manager Will Venable another explosive bat as part of a streaky White Sox lineup, posting an .841 OPS with 20 home runs, 45 RBI, 36 runs scored, and one stolen base through 70 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Andrew Benintendi blasts grand slam in win over Yankees
desc: Andrew Benintendi went 1-for-1 in a 5-1 win over the Yankees with a grand slam.
impact: Benintendi has heated up at the plate, driving in runs in four of his last six contests. The veteran remains one of many streaky options in the White Sox lineup to this point, slashing .242 with nine home runs, 37 RBI, 30 runs scored, and one stolen base across 66 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Sean Burke cruises on mound in win over Yankees
desc: Sean Burke allowed one earned run on five hits and one walk while striking out eight over 7 1/3 innings in Thursday's win over the Yankees.
impact: Burke continues a solid stretch on the mound of late, allowing two earned runs or less in four of his last six trips to the mound. The right-hander has offered manager Will Venable one of the more stable options every fifth day, carrying a 3.89 ERA and 1.22 WHIP with a 4-4 record and 9.0 K/9 ratio through 15 appearances.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Ryan McMahon homers in loss to White Sox
desc: Ryan McMahon went 1-for-3 in Thursday's loss to the White Sox with a solo home run.
impact: McMahon has offered mixed results at the plate of late, picking up hits in six of his last 13 contests. The infielder remains one of the more underwhelming options in the Yankees lineup for manager Aaron Boone, hitting .211 with eight home runs, 23 RBI, 19 runs scored, and three stolen bases across 67 games.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Juan Soto launches pair of homers
desc: Juan Soto went 2-for-4 with two solo home runs and a walk in Thursday's 6-4 win over the Phillies. He opened the scoring with a first-inning homer off Aaron Nola before taking Nola deep again in his next plate appearance. It was Soto's second multi-homer game of the season.
impact: Soto is 14-for-29 with three home runs over his last eight games. He is slashing .300/.398/.582 with 17 home runs, seven doubles, one triple, 38 RBI, 36 runs, and six stolen bases across 249 plate appearances this season.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Devin Williams records 11th save
desc: Devin Williams earned the save Thursday against the Phillies, allowing one run on two hits and one walk while striking out one over one inning. He entered with a three-run lead in the ninth and allowed a run on a Justin Crawford RBI single before preventing further damage.
impact: Williams secured his 11th save of the season and has recorded scoreless outings in 16 of his last 18 appearances. He owns a 5.18 ERA, 1.56 WHIP, and 38:15 K:BB across 24.1 innings.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Sean Manaea takes no-decision against Phillies
desc: Sean Manaea did not factor into the decision Thursday against the Phillies, allowing three runs, two earned, on six hits and one walk over 5.1 innings. He struck out five while throwing 63 of his 95 pitches for strikes and generating 16 whiffs. Philadelphia scored in the first, third, and fourth innings, with the final run coming home after a throwing error by AJ Ewing.
impact: Manaea was making just his second start of the season and appears likely to remain in the rotation moving forward. His next scheduled start is set to come at home against the Cubs.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Ryan Weathers sharp in no-decision
desc: Ryan Weathers allowed one earned run on three hits and one walk while striking out eight over 6 1/3 innings in Thursday's loss to the White Sox.
impact: Weathers has struggled to miss opposing bats of late, allowing five earned runs or more in four of his last six starts. The left-hander has been difficult to trust as part of a deep Yankees starting staff for manager Aaron Boone after a strong start to the season, carrying a 4.13 ERA and 1.13 WHIP with a 2-5 record and 9.9 K/9 ratio across 14 starts this season.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Marcus Semien drives in two with triple Thursday
desc: Marcus Semien went 2-for-4 with a two-run triple in Thursday's win over the Phillies. He delivered the key hit of the game in the seventh inning, ripping a two-out triple off Jose Alvarado to extend New York's lead from 4-3 to 6-3. Semien also added a single in the victory.
impact: Semien is now slashing .225/.283/.362 with nine home runs, 26 RBI, and six stolen bases through 298 plate appearances in his first season with the Mets.

author: Nate Miller
title: Bryson Stott steals a base, scores a run Thursday night
desc: Bryson Stott went 1-for-3 with a walk, a steal, and one run scored in Thursday's 6-4 loss to the Mets.
impact: Stott continues to swing a hot bat. The 28-year-old second baseman has hit safely in 9 of 11 games, posting a .342/.432/.500 slash line with four doubles, one triple, eight RBI, and four steals in that span.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Jack Leiter takes third straight loss
desc: Jack Leiter (3-7) took the loss Thursday against the Twins after allowing six runs on seven hits and two walks over four innings. He struck out four. Minnesota scored four runs in the first inning, including a three-run homer by Brooks Lee, before Trevor Larnach added a two-run shot in the fourth.
impact: Leiter has lost three straight starts while allowing 15 earned runs over 13.2 innings. He owns a 5.29 ERA, 1.44 WHIP, and 83:35 K:BB across 80 innings, with his next start tentatively lined up for next week in Miami.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Wyatt Langford launches homer in loss to Twins
desc: Wyatt Langford went 2-for-4 with a walk and a solo home run in Thursday's 9-3 loss to Minnesota. He led off the sixth inning with his second homer in four games, giving Texas its first run of the night.
impact: Langford has hit safely in five of his last six games, batting .375/.400/.667 with four RBI and four runs during that stretch after a slow start following his return from the injured list in early June.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Shea Langeliers goes deep in win over Angels
desc: Shea Langeliers went 1-for-4 in a win over the Angels with a three-run home run.
impact: Langeliers continues a solid stretch at the plate, picking up hits in 12 of his last 15 contests. The catcher remains one of the more explosive options in the Athletics lineup, carrying an .870 OPS with 19 home runs, 39 RBI, 48 runs scored, and one stolen base across 68 games.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Ezequiel Duran homers in loss to Twins
desc: Ezequiel Duran went 1-for-3 with a solo home run in Thursday's 9-3 loss to the Twins. The homer was his fifth of the season and first in 24 games. It also snapped a six-game stretch without an RBI.
impact: Duran ranks second on the Rangers with 37 RBI through 65 games and will remain a lineup regular. He is expected to continue seeing time at shortstop while Corey Seager is unavailable with a concussion, with second base also in play once Seager returns.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Justin Foscue homers off bench Thursday
desc: Justin Foscue went 1-for-1 with a home run and a walk in two plate appearances off the bench against the Twins on Thursday. The homer continued a productive stretch for the infielder, who is batting .274/.333/.493 through 81 plate appearances this season.
impact: Foscue has been limited primarily to starts against left-handed pitching since the Rangers added Nicky Lopez. His playing-time outlook could become even more crowded with Josh Smith back in the lineup.
